segments.text: This pan doesn't stick, but the chemicals do. A new study linked a chemical used in non-stick pans to an increased risk of fatty liver disease in kids. The chemical is called PFOA. In this study, when levels doubled, kids showed a 169% increased risk of fatty liver disease and it [music] got worse with age. Why are kids so vulnerable?

Forever. Chemicals are known to cause metabolic and endocrine disruption. During adolescence, hormones are changing and the body is growing rapidly. This makes kids and young adults especially vulnerable to the endocrine hormonal and metabolic damage caused by these forever chemicals.

Despite this, PAS are still used everywhere in cookware, clothing, and even electronics. This study does have limitations, but the takeaway is simple. Avoiding non-stick and choosing cookware without PAS, such as a stainless steel, is a much safer bet. I hope this message sticks.
